To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter
Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of
Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and
look forward to your mark-up.
SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.
Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and
only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the
basket is recoverable.
Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after
Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims
unless expressly stated otherwise.
Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same
caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.
Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and
non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.
Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public
registers (see Disclosure Letter).
Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the

public records.
Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller
will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the
counterparty's written consent.
Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding)
will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds
flow.)
Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio
matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.
Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter

above.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and
records are fictional.
1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the
indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including
DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly
searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific
disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent,
payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.
2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause
11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final
written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.
3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2.
As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security
is included.
4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of
every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of
non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or

person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation

loss amount.

Buyer has completed its own verification.

must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer-Side Review of the Seller's Draft

## Bottom line

The Seller's package is built to shift nearly all risk to Wattlebridge. It combines a low general cap, a high threshold, short time limits, whole-data-room disclosure, and a buyer-knowledge bar. Several issues the Seller has already identified, including Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, the employee bonuses, and the privacy incident, would then fall outside any warranty recovery. The Seller's own disclosure letter confirms these are live. Known matters need to be resolved through price, debt-like deductions, conditions precedent, or specific indemnities. Leaving them to the warranty regime would leave Wattlebridge with little or no recovery.

I have worked from the Seller's summary positions and disclosure letter, not the full SPA text, so clause-level drafting should be checked against the actual mark-up.

## Part A: Where the Seller departs from Wattlebridge's interests

### 1. Risk allocation architecture

**a) General cap at 20% (AUD 4.8m) (Cl 12.1).** This is the Seller's ceiling for general warranty claims, and the arithmetic is correct. It is low for a AUD 24m deal with a known pipeline of issues. The known exposures in the Seller's own disclosures already total roughly AUD 4.1m before any privacy-related loss (see table below), so the cap would be largely consumed by matters we already know about.

*Push back:* A general cap of at least 30–50% of price, with fundamental and tax warranties at 100% of price. Ask the Seller to justify 20% against the disclosed exposures.

**b) Threshold structure (Cl 12.2).** A AUD 25k de minimis, plus a AUD 250k basket with excess-only recovery, means the first AUD 250k of aggregate claims is unrecoverable. Each claim below AUD 25k also falls away entirely. The basket is about 1% of price, and the excess-only structure means that for a AUD 300k loss Wattlebridge recovers only AUD 50k.

*Push back:* De minimis at AUD 10k (with aggregation of related claims), a tipping basket (first-dollar recovery once exceeded) of no more than about 0.5% of price, and no threshold at all for fundamental, tax, and specific-indemnity claims.

**c) Time limits (Cl 12.3/13).** General warranty claims must be notified within 18 months. The Seller then proposes that any limitation applies to all claims unless expressly carved out. That gap matters because several issues, including privacy, tax, and Ironquay IP title, may not crystallise within 18 months.

*Push back:*
- General warranties: 24–36 months.
- Fundamental warranties (capacity, title, shares): 6 years, or the statutory limitation period, which is 6 years for contract claims under the *Limitation Act 1969* (NSW) and may be 12 years if the SPA is executed as a deed. Confirm with NSW counsel.
- Tax: the ATO amendment period plus a buffer (for example, 60 days after it expires).
- Specific indemnities: until the relevant matter is resolved, plus a buffer.

**d) Fundamental and title warranties on the same caps and time limits (Cl 12.1–13).** This is a clear error. Capacity and title are binary warranties that go to whether the Seller can deliver what it is selling. They should not be treated as "administrative simplicity" matters.

*Push back:* Fundamental warranties (title to shares, capacity, authority, no insolvency) should be capped at the full purchase price with the longest limitation period. Tax warranties and a pre-Completion tax indemnity should sit outside the general regime.

**e) Limitations and exclusive remedy apply to "all Claims of any nature" (Cl 9.3, 12.8, 20.5).** This would catch fraud, fundamental warranties, specific indemnities, and any statutory claims.

*Push back:* Carve out:
- fraud (which generally cannot be excluded by contract)
- fundamental warranties
- tax
- specific indemnities
- conduct that may breach the Australian Consumer Law (Sch 2, *Competition and Consumer Act 2010* (Cth)), particularly misleading or deceptive conduct

Non-reliance wording should be drafted so it does not purport to exclude fraud or statutory liability. Confirm the position with NSW counsel.

### 2. Disclosure and knowledge

**f) General disclosure of the entire data room and public registers (Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2; Schedule 7).** The letter discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the data room as at 22 September 2026 (DD-002 to DD-012), plus the Accounts, statutory registers, and public searches. This effectively negates the warranties. Wattlebridge would be deemed to have accepted everything in the data room, including the known issues, and the Seller's counsel would argue that any warranty breach was disclosed.

*Push back:* Delete general disclosure. Accept only specific, fair disclosure against specifically identified warranties, with reasonable detail. Documents should be disclosed only if specifically referred to and attached, not by data room reference. Public register disclosure should be limited to the specific matter.

**g) Buyer-knowledge bar (Cl 8.3).** The Buyer has no claim in respect of any matter known to the Buyer or its advisers, including anything discoverable from the data room. Combined with the general disclosure, this would bar almost every claim, because the Seller is relying on the data room as its disclosure.

*Push back:* Include a pro-sandbagging clause: Wattlebridge's knowledge does not prejudice its claims. The NSW position on sandbagging is not settled, so the protection should be express. At minimum, the knowledge bar should not apply to matters the Seller has specifically disclosed as unresolved (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses, privacy). Those should be dealt with through specific indemnities, not warranty claims.

### 3. Known issues

The Seller has identified the following. Each needs a specific fix.

| Issue | Seller's position | Exposure (AUD, indicative) | Buyer position |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ironquay SOW3 (DD-004 cl 7.3; DD-010) | Indemnity limited to SOW3 fee; "adequate" | 180,000 open, plus IP title risk on SOW3 Project Materials | Pay the 180k pre-Completion (or deduct it); obtain Ironquay's confirmatory IP assignment as a CP; uncapped specific indemnity for all Ironquay fees and IP claims |
| Riverlark facility (DD-003) | Release "following Completion" | ~3,200,000 outstanding; no discharge | Repay at Completion from the price as debt; payoff letter and PPSR discharge as completion deliverables |
| Bluefen consent (DD-002, cl 11.2–11.3) | Treat as satisfied on delivery of counterparty consent; reasonable endeavours | Bluefen ~30% of FY26 revenue (~3,600,000) | Unconditional written consent with conditions 11.3 satisfied as a CP; walk right if not obtained; best endeavours; consider MAC or price protection |
| Employee bonuses (DD-005) | "A matter for the Seller"; not in funds flow | 420,000, plus super and payroll tax (indicatively ~70–75k at current NSW rates; confirm) | Treat as debt-like; Seller bears all amounts including on-costs |
| Privacy/export incident (DD-006; Sch 6; cl 4.6) | "Preliminary, not expected to be material" | ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps); no loss quantified | Pre-Completion forensic investigation at Seller cost; uncapped specific indemnity for notification, regulatory, and third-party losses; no disclosure against privacy warranties |
| Supplier renewals (DD-008, DD-011) | "Ordinary course" | 330,000 aggregate (3 × 110,000) | Confirm whether committed, accrued, or terminable; treat accrued amounts as debt-like; buyer approval of renewals pre-Completion |
| Office lease (DD-007) | Notification obligation only | Unquantified | Landlord consent or estoppel as CP, or specific indemnity |
| Mossvale (DD-009) | Restriction on assignment; no consent stated as required | Unquantified | Written confirmation that no consent is required, or consent as CP |
| Title (DD-012) | Share register as evidence | Fundamental | Full verification: ASIC search, original certificates, PPSR search over shares, and register rectification if needed; title as a fundamental warranty |
| Tax and IP | "Settled under the general regime" | Unquantified | Standalone tax warranties and pre-Completion tax indemnity outside the general regime; IP warranties with appropriate protection |

**Quantifying the gap.** The known, disclosed items add up to roughly AUD 4.1m before privacy losses, which is close to the entire general cap of AUD 4.8m. Several of them would also fall under the AUD 25k de minimis or AUD 250k basket if they were pursued as warranty claims. They should be addressed through the price mechanism and specific indemnities, not left to warranty recovery.

### 4. Funds flow and price mechanics

- The funds flow "reflects the agreed price mechanics" but omits the bonuses (cl 5 of the letter). It should show all debt and debt-like items, including Riverlark repayment, bonuses with on-costs, Ironquay fees, and any accrued supplier obligations.
- Ask for a locked-box or completion accounts mechanism to be confirmed. The "debt-free/cash-free" baseline must include a working capital adjustment, and debt definitions should capture break costs, fees, and any guarantees.
- Confirm whether the AUD 24m is adjusted for any debt-like items before the Seller's proposed net figures are accepted.

### 5. Drafting and consistency points

- Clause references are inconsistent across the documents (for example, Riverlark appears under Cl 2/7 and Bluefen under Cl 3/6.3). Ask the Seller to reconcile them before the mark-up.
- The "no admission" wording (Disclosure Letter 1.4) and the reservation (11) are acceptable as boilerplate, provided they do not override specific indemnities or allow the Seller to argue that disclosure of an issue means no breach.
- The Seller's statement that the privacy matter is "not expected to be material" is an opinion, not a fact. It should not be accepted as a characterisation in the SPA.

### 6. Timing point on the privacy incident

Under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme (Part IIIC, *Privacy Act 1988* (Cth)), an eligible data breach requires notification to the OAIC and affected individuals as soon as practicable, with an assessment expected within 30 days of awareness. The data room document is dated September 2026 and today is 6 November 2026. Whether the 30-day assessment window has already run needs urgent confirmation. Wattlebridge should not take on a company whose notification compliance is unclear without a specific indemnity and a pre-Completion investigation.

## Part B: Summary of recommendations

**Priority 1: must-have before signing**
1. Remove general data room disclosure; allow only specific, fair disclosure.
2. Add a pro-sandbagging clause and carve out known matters from the knowledge bar.
3. Carve out fraud, fundamental warranties, tax, and specific indemnities from all limitations and exclusive-remedy provisions.
4. Separate the fundamental warranties (title, capacity) with a full-price cap and 6-year period.
5. Specific uncapped indemnities for the privacy incident, Ironquay, and the bonuses.
6. Bluefen unconditional consent as a condition precedent, with a walk right.
7. Riverlark repaid at Completion from the price, with discharge documents as completion deliverables.

**Priority 2: price and mechanics**
8. Treat the AUD 420k bonuses (plus on-costs), AUD 180k Ironquay balance, and accrued supplier obligations as debt-like items, deducted from the price.
9. Redraft the funds flow to show all debt and debt-like items.
10. Verify title independently (ASIC, PPSR, certificates).

**Priority 3: commercial protection**
11. General cap of 30–50% of price; de minimis AUD 10k; tipping basket at around 0.5% of price.
12. General warranty period of 24–36 months; tax to the ATO amendment period plus buffer.
13. Standalone tax warranties and pre-Completion tax indemnity.
14. Landlord consent or estoppel (lease) and written confirmation on Mossvale.
15. Pre-Completion forensic review of the privacy incident, at Seller cost.

**Next steps**
- Obtain the full SPA text and Disclosure Letter clauses so the mark-up can be drafted against the actual wording.
- Instruct NSW counsel to confirm the limitation periods, sandbagging position, and ACL and non-reliance analysis.
- Have a privacy specialist confirm the NDB timeline and whether an eligible data breach has occurred.
- Ask the Seller to reconcile the clause numbering and provide the Ironquay, Bluefen, and Riverlark correspondence.
